primary_offense_summary: Companies failing to pay proper wages, overtime, or compensation for meal breaks, enforced by DOL Wage and Hour Division.
Companies failing to give 60-day advance notice to workers before mass layoffs or plant closings as required by the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act.
Mismanagement of employee retirement and benefit plans (pensions, 401k) including ERISA violations such as using underperforming proprietary funds or denying proper protections.
Employers terminating, retaliating against, or failing to reinstate employees who take protected medical or family leave under the FMLA.
Employers discriminating against job applicants or employees based on race, gender, age, national origin, disability, or other protected characteristics.
Employers violating Fair Credit Reporting Act requirements during hiring, such as failing to provide proper notice before obtaining background reports on applicants.
Unfair labor practices cases brought by the NLRB, primarily resulting in back pay awards for violations of workers collective bargaining and organizing rights.
Employers retaliating against employees who report safety violations, fraud, or other wrongdoing to regulators or authorities, violating whistleblower protection laws.
Employers unlawfully employing undocumented workers, misusing H-1B or other visa programs, or discriminating against U.S. workers in favor of foreign visa holders.
State AG and FTC enforcement for deceptive marketing, false advertising, and unfair business practices that harm consumers.
High-interest short-term lenders making illegal loans, charging unauthorized fees, misrepresenting terms, or operating without proper state licenses.
Large-scale mortgage servicing and foreclosure abuses by major banks, including improper foreclosures on servicemembers and falsification of documents.
Cannabis businesses failing to maintain proper state licenses, inventory controls, security measures, or product testing requirements.
Casinos and gaming companies failing to comply with gambling regulations, including paying winnings to self-excluded problem gamblers or failing to disclose principal suitability issues.
Insurers using non-compliant policy forms, discriminating against certain health conditions, using unlicensed agents, or improperly calculating premiums.
Landlords and property owners failing to maintain safe and habitable conditions for tenants or allowing foreclosed properties to fall into disrepair.
Data breaches, biometric data violations (BIPA), improper collection or sharing of personal information, and Do Not Call registry violations.
Companies failing to provide equal access to goods and services for individuals with disabilities, including physical access, service animals, and digital accessibility.
Companies discriminating against customers based on protected characteristics in insurance pricing, lending, or other consumer-facing services.
FCC enforcement for improper device marketing, unauthorized transmission, 911 outage failures, and improper pricing to schools.
State PUC enforcement against electric and broadband utilities for service reliability failures, outages, and failure to meet operating performance standards.
DOT enforcement against airlines for failing to provide timely refunds, violating tarmac delay rules, and failing to accommodate passengers with disabilities.
State and local enforcement for using properties in violation of land use and zoning laws, including unpermitted commercial uses and university land use violations.
HUD and state enforcement for failures to comply with Home Mortgage Disclosure Act reporting requirements and affordable housing program rules.
Credit bureaus, tenant screeners, and insurers violating FCRA by reporting inaccurate information, failing to notify consumers, or improperly using credit reports.
OSHA enforcement for hazardous working conditions including mine explosions, failure to protect workers from toxic exposures, and pandemic-related safety failures.
MSHA enforcement for violations of federal mine safety and health standards at coal and other mines.
FRA enforcement for violations of federal railroad safety standards covering track, equipment, and operating practices.
FAA enforcement for aviation safety violations including improper hazardous materials shipping and aircraft maintenance deficiencies.
NHTSA enforcement for violations of federal motor vehicle safety standards by auto manufacturers and equipment suppliers.
DOJ enforcement against private prisoner transport companies for violations of the Interstate Transportation of Dangerous Criminals Act.
NRC and DOE enforcement for violations of nuclear safety regulations at facilities using or handling radioactive materials.
FERC enforcement for violations of hydroelectric project licenses and dam safety regulations, including structural safety failures.
State PUC and PHMSA enforcement for gas pipeline safety violations, inadequate maintenance procedures, and incidents causing fatalities or property damage.
Banks and financial institutions failing to maintain adequate AML compliance programs, monitor suspicious transactions, or file required suspicious activity reports.
Federal and state banking regulator enforcement for unfair or deceptive practices, unsafe mortgage servicing, failure to register, and other bank regulatory violations.
Companies violating OFAC sanctions by conducting business with sanctioned countries, entities, or individuals such as Iran, Cuba, or designated persons.
Criminal cases involving companies actively concealing or moving proceeds of illegal activity through financial transactions.
Misconduct related to mortgage-backed securities and structured financial products, primarily arising from the 2008 financial crisis (RMBS, CDOs, repurchase claims).
SEC and CFTC enforcement for failures to protect investors, including inadequate disclosures, improper fund management, and failure to segregate customer assets.
FINRA and state securities regulator enforcement for improper IPO share sales, unregistered securities offerings (including crypto), and trading rule violations.
Trading securities based on material non-public information, criminally prosecuted or settled with the SEC (e.g., SAC Capital).
DOJ Trustee Program enforcement against banks for filing fraudulent claims in bankruptcy proceedings, and consultants for inadequate conflict-of-interest disclosures.
SEC enforcement for falsifying financial statements, overstating revenue, or manipulating accounting records to mislead investors.
State and local tax compliance failures including failure to pay business registration fees, tax underpayments, and offers in compromise.
General fraud violations including overbilling government clients, fraudulently obtaining contracts set aside for small businesses, and FHA mortgage fraud.
Companies bribing foreign government officials to obtain or retain business abroad, violating FCPA anti-bribery and books-and-records provisions.
Companies providing improper financial incentives to healthcare providers, government officials, or others to generate business or referrals.
RICO violations involving organized criminal schemes by businesses, such as enlisting shoplifters to supply stolen goods for resale.
Enforcement for violations of postal regulations and laws governing the use of the U.S. mail system.
Criminal enforcement for destroying documents, harassment campaigns, or conspiring to obstruct federal investigations or court proceedings.
Criminal and civil enforcement for making false statements to federal agencies, financial institutions, or in connection with government contracts.
Criminal theft violations by corporations, including theft from suppliers in processing operations.
DOJ enforcement against companies that violated prior antitrust consent decrees or court orders issued in connection with mergers and acquisitions.
Civil litigation for publishing or broadcasting false statements that harm reputation (e.g., Fox News/Dominion Voting Systems).
Criminal cases of companies or individuals stealing proprietary business information, often involving foreign actors stealing U.S. technology.
Copyright infringement, trafficking in counterfeit goods, and Digital Millennium Copyright Act violations.
DOJ and state AG antitrust enforcement for bid-rigging, price-fixing conspiracies, predatory pricing, and monopolistic conduct harming competition.
FERC and CFTC enforcement for manipulation of electricity and natural gas markets, submitting false capacity data, and reporting false trading information.
BIS and State Department enforcement for exporting controlled technology or military equipment to prohibited countries or parties without authorization.
Customs fraud including undervaluing imported goods to avoid paying duties, importing merchandise without examination, and other customs compliance failures.
USDA enforcement for violations of agricultural marketing and grading standards, including camera grading installation requirements and grain security violations.
Coast Guard and DOT enforcement for maritime safety violations including vessel accidents, boiler explosions, and collisions causing damage or fatalities.
CBP and DOJ enforcement for undervaluing imported goods, mislabeling merchandise, and other schemes to fraudulently avoid paying customs duties.
Violations of the requirement that goods shipped between U.S. ports be carried on U.S.-built, U.S.-flagged, U.S.-owned, and U.S.-crewed vessels.
DOJ enforcement against government contractors and healthcare providers for submitting fraudulent claims for payment to federal programs.
DOI enforcement against oil and gas companies for failing to properly report production volumes and pay royalties owed on federal land leases.

primary_offense: off-label or unapproved promotion of medical products
primary_offense_summary: DOJ and FDA enforcement against pharmaceutical companies for marketing drugs for unapproved uses, frequently tied to opioid and other drug marketing scandals.
DEA enforcement for pharmacy and hospital failures to properly track, report, or secure controlled substances, and drug distribution abuse.

primary_offense: Medicare Parts C and D Enforcement Action
primary_offense_summary: CMS enforcement against Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plan sponsors for improper contract administration and required beneficiary notice failures.
HHS OIG enforcement for violations of healthcare fraud and abuse laws, including employing excluded individuals and self-disclosed billing violations.

primary_offense: Medicare Coverage Gap Discount Program violation
primary_offense_summary: CMS enforcement against drug manufacturers for violations of Medicare Part D Coverage Gap Discount Program pricing requirements.
CMS enforcement for patient care deficiencies at skilled nursing facilities including substandard care, staffing failures, and safety violations.
Federal and state enforcement for billing patients improperly, failing to disclose pricing, or wrongly charging for services patients qualified to receive free.
State AG enforcement against bioscience companies for illegally buying, selling, or transferring fetal tissue in violation of state or federal law.
FEC and state enforcement for improper corporate political contributions, failure to disclose political advertising expenditures, and campaign finance law violations.
Enforcement for failure to file required regulatory reports including CFIUS foreign ownership disclosures and lobbying contribution disclosure reports.
DOJ enforcement against companies (e.g., Chiquita, Lafarge) that made payments to organizations designated as terrorist groups.
DOJ enforcement for unauthorized access to competitor or third-party computer systems to steal proprietary data.
State Department enforcement for unauthorized transfer of classified military technology or data to foreign countries.

primary_offense: unlawful receipt of sex trafficking proceeds
primary_offense_summary: DOJ enforcement against companies (e.g., Pornhub parent Aylo) that received and retained proceeds from sex trafficking operations.
Civil and criminal enforcement against companies that facilitated or financially benefited from sexual exploitation of children (e.g., JPMorgan/Epstein).
Civil litigation against firearms manufacturers for marketing weapons in ways that facilitate violence, and enforcement against unlicensed ghost gun companies.

primary_offense: drug or medical equipment safety violation
primary_offense_summary: Companies selling defective drugs or medical devices, distributing adulterated medications, or misrepresenting product safety to the FDA.
Companies failing to report defective consumer products to CPSC, selling harmful products, or failing to issue timely recalls (e.g., defective combat earplugs, JUUL).
Food manufacturers shipping contaminated products linked to illness outbreaks, violating FDA food safety regulations (e.g., listeria, salmonella contamination).
Lawsuits and enforcement against tobacco companies for selling to minors, violating the 1998 Master Settlement Agreement, or deceptive marketing practices.

primary_offense: Clery Act campus security reporting violation
primary_offense_summary: Department of Education fines against universities for failing to properly disclose campus crimes and mishandling sexual assault cases (e.g., Michigan State/Nassar, Penn State/Sandusky).
EPA enforcement for improper handling or disposal of asbestos at demolition or construction sites, and litigation for concealing asbestos health risks.
NHTSA fines against automakers for failing to meet Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards for their passenger car or light truck fleets.
EPA Clean Air Act enforcement for air emissions violations, storm water management failures, and violations of air quality permits at industrial facilities.
Safe Drinking Water Act enforcement for monitoring failures, nitrate contamination, and violations at public water supply systems.
Litigation and enforcement for contamination of groundwater with methyl tertiary-butyl ether (MTBE), a gasoline additive linked to health risks.
EPA enforcement and civil litigation for contamination of waterways and communities from polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), primarily against Monsanto.
Litigation and enforcement for contaminating water supplies with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS or forever chemicals), primarily from firefighting foam.
EPA enforcement against large livestock operations (CAFOs and feedlots) for water pollution and other environmental violations.
EPA, Coast Guard, and state enforcement for oil spills from vessels and pipelines, including failure to accurately report spills and clean up contamination.
EPA Clean Water Act enforcement for discharging pollutants including coal ash and industrial wastewater into rivers, lakes, and other waterways.
Litigation for contamination from radioactive waste at nuclear weapons and fuel facilities, and state radiation control law violations.
EPA RCRA enforcement for improper storage, handling, or disposal of hazardous waste at manufacturing and industrial facilities.
EPA and state enforcement for violations of underground petroleum storage tank regulations, including failure to test, repair, or shut down non-compliant tanks.
BSEE enforcement for offshore oil and gas drilling safety violations, including equipment failures, crane accidents, and inoperative safety systems.
DOT/PHMSA enforcement for pipeline safety regulation violations, including fatal incidents caused by corrosion, inadequate inspection, or improper design.
Federal enforcement for disturbing, excavating, or removing archaeological resources from public or tribal lands without authorization.
EPA and state enforcement for environmental damage from mining operations including water quality violations and natural resource damage.
EPA FIFRA enforcement for distributing or selling pesticides without required labels, without a state license, or in violation of federal registration requirements.
State environmental enforcement for violations of solid waste management regulations at disposal facilities and industrial operations.
Enforcement and litigation for products containing excessive lead levels including childrens jewelry, school supplies, and lead-based paint.
DOE enforcement for failures to comply with mandatory energy efficiency standards for appliances and equipment.
USDA and DOJ enforcement for violations of the Animal Welfare Act at research facilities, breeders, and animal dealers.
